key_insight: AISPA is a user-centric framework that audits hidden system prompts in commercial AI products and shows that protective and problematic instructions often coexist.
engineering_relevance: For AI system builders, the paper highlights the need for transparent, standardized prompt governance to reduce user-risk and improve accountability.
method: Defines an 8-dimension AISPA taxonomy for prompt auditing
Classifies 3,249 system-prompt instructions from 88 commercial AI products as protective or problematic
Compares prompt design patterns across products and developers
evidence_signal: The audit covers 3,249 instructions from 88 commercial AI products and finds that 98.9% of products include at least one protective instruction, but only 24% cover all eight AISPA dimensions.
watch_item: The framework depends on prompt access and human/criteria-based classification, so results may be incomplete or harder to reproduce when prompts are undisclosed or frequently updated.
paper_title: AISPA: User-Centric System Prompt Auditing for Large Language Model Applications
